youtube_title: Michigan City's Old Lighthouse: Harriet Colfax, her assistants and 43 years at the light
body: In 1861, Harriet Colfax took charge of Michigan City's lighthouse, and she kept the light burning for 43 years, living there with her lifelong companion, Ann Hartwell. In 1871 a pier light was added, and through 1882 five assistant keepers served with her: two women and three men. In 1873 she wrote in her log, "A terrible hurricane to-night." Until a storm took the pier light in 1886, she tended it too, even when waves broke over the walkway and ice coated it. She retired in 1904 at about 80. That year she said, "I could not bear to see anyone else light my lamp." She died the next spring. Her 1858 lighthouse still stands as the Old Lighthouse Museum, open April through October, Wednesday to Sunday. Updated version: thanks to the viewer who reminded us she had assistant keepers. 🌊 Comment your town, and it could be next! #MichiganCity #LaPorteCounty #Lighthouse #LakeMichigan #Indiana #History #LaPorteAfterDark
